question: Explain the Efficient Market Hypothesis and its three forms. What does it imply for investors?
sources: Fama, E. F. (1970), 'Efficient Capital Markets: A Review of Theory and Empirical Work', Journal of Finance

points.label: Meaning
points.description: In an efficient market, security prices quickly and fully reflect available information, so no investor can consistently earn above-normal returns after adjusting for risk.
points.basis: Fama (1970): definition of an efficient market

points.label: Weak form
points.description: Prices reflect all past price and volume information, so price changes follow a random walk and technical analysis cannot give consistent excess returns.

points.label: Semi-strong form
points.description: Prices reflect all publicly available information, such as results, announcements and economic news, so fundamental analysis of public data cannot give consistent excess returns.

points.label: Strong form
points.description: Prices reflect all information, public and private, so even insiders cannot earn excess returns; this form is generally not supported, which is why insider trading is prohibited.

points.label: Implications and limits
points.description: Investors in efficient markets may prefer diversified, passive strategies; evidence of anomalies and behavioural biases means markets are not perfectly efficient.
points.basis: Financial economics literature on market anomalies and behavioural finance
